body:
## Problem

`flow._publish_bundle` (`template/src/pdca_harness/flow.py:642-665` on branch `fix/593-stack-mode-append-only-fold-real-base-prs`) decides "pushed this run" from `publish.json`'s mtime. When `publish.publish` **raises** after the push but before `publish.json` is written, the bundle is held even though its branch is on origin. One way: `gh` is missing, so `subprocess.run(pr_cmd)` raises `FileNotFoundError` (`publish.py:386`).

This errs toward holding on purpose (the docstring says so: "nor does a call that raised … that errs toward holding"), and the round-5 code review called it safe. But it differs from the stated rule "a branch pushed this run is folded" (`flow.py:1887-1888`): its dependents are skipped although their prerequisite is on origin, and the operator is not told that the branch was pushed.

## Done when

Decide one of: (a) record the push itself (e.g. write a marker or the pushed SHA right after the push succeeds) so a later exception still counts as pushed; or (b) keep holding, and make the stderr line say the branch may already be on origin and how to resume. Pin the choice with a test that raises from `gh pr create` after the push.

Found by the eduralph/pdca-pdca Act review of 2026-10-02 (issue_593 iteration-v5 code review).
title: flow: publish that raises after the push holds the bundle though its branch is on origin, and does not say so
